bug_semantics: The Yandex Lockbox secrets backend in Apache Airflow's Yandex provider (providers/yandex/.../secrets/lockbox.py) tried the team-scoped lookup first and, on a miss, fell through to the team-agnostic secret name. The guard meant to stop a caller naming another team's secret (`_is_team_specific_accessed_as_global`) had `team_name is None` as its first condition, so it did nothing whenever a team scope was supplied — exactly the case that matters. A caller authorized for one team could supply an id spelling out another team's namespace and resolve that team's Connection or Variable, obtaining its credentials in full (CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key).
flaw_origin: Commit 86806861cc0d30b75554315f4832a566a9fb3a0c ("Add multi-team lookup to Lockbox backend (#65695)", 2026-04-23, author PrithviBadiga <45932166+PrithviBadiga@users.noreply.github.com>, committer GitHub) introduced the whole multi-team flow: team-scoped lookup first, then `if not secret: secret = self._find_secret(secrets, prefix, key)` — the team-agnostic fall-through — guarded only by `_is_team_specific_accessed_as_global`, whose first condition `team_name is None` neutralizes the guard precisely when a team scope is present. The advisory's named sink (the fall-through plus its broken guard) is written by this commit; parent 6dcfb1a7c7 has no team handling in the backend. The team_name parameter on the public methods came earlier from d32091cd4f4b (#58905, Vincent, 2025-12-10) but was then unused (no team handling at all in the body) — not a bypass yet.

Parent 6dcfb1a7c7: get_conn_value/get_variable accept team_name (added unused by d32091cd4f4b) but contain no team lookup and no fall-through.', 'Fix commit 0d877a1a7680 (2026-08-01, Jarek Potiuk, #70877 "Refuse the team agnostic fall-through for a team scoped Lockbox secret name"): replaces `_is_team_specific_accessed_as_global` with `_names_a_team_namespace(secret_id)` (no team_name clause — refused for every lookup), adds `_log_refusal`, settling ambiguity before any name is built; the commit message itself diagnoses the broken guard: "its first condition is team_name is None, so it does nothing whenever a team scope is supplied -- exactly when it matters".', "Version boundary: BIC 86806861cc0d first tagged providers-yandex/4.5.0 (4.5.0rc1); fix 0d877a1a7680 contained in providers-yandex/4.5.1 (4.5.1rc1/rc2), matching the advisory's fixed version apache-airflow-providers-yandex 4.5.1.", "AI-marker screening: `git log --format='%an <%ae>%n%cn <%ce>%n%B' -1` on 86806861cc0d and d32091cd4f4b — human authors only; grep for claude/copilot/anthropic/openai/generated/co-authored/cursor/junie finds nothing (NONE sentinels). The FIX commit 0d877a1a7680 carries 'Generated-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context)' per Airflow's AI-assisted-contribution policy — recorded here, but fix-object markers never attribute flaw origin (BIC-only attribution rule)."] Squash decomposition verified 2026-08-29: introducer is a member commit of a GitHub squash landing; decomposed_shas=['d32091cd4f4b2b0935bc71e02e2995cdb8713a30'] verified via clone/PR-head ancestry and first-write diff.
reasoning: Vulnerability first: the advisory names the team-agnostic fall-through after a missed team-scoped lookup; the pre-fix code shows it verbatim (`if not secret: secret = self._find_secret(secrets, prefix, key)`) with a guard whose `team_name is None` clause voids it for team-scoped calls, and the fix replaces the guard with a team-agnostic refusal — proving the fall-through with the broken guard is the defect. BIC choice: 86806861cc0d (#65695) created the named sink — the fall-through and its broken guard — and its parent has neither; the earlier d32091cd4f4b only added an unused team_name parameter and introduced no bypass, so it sits in decomposed_shas as the wave that set up the multi-team interface. Squash handling: the flaw spans the multi-team feature over the pre-existing team_name interface, so squash_decomposed=true.
